Rostec will present the Russian fifth-generation Su-57E fighter in its export configuration at the El Alamein International Airshow 2026 in Egypt, featuring fundamentally new weapons that have never previously been demonstrated in Russia or abroad.
Rostec is likely referring to the new S-71K “Kovyor” and S-71M “Monokhrom,” small, low-observable, jet-powered cruise missile/UAVs designed to be launched from Russian Su-57 multirole fighters.
The El Alamein International Airshow 2026 will take place at El Alamein International Airport, Egypt, from September 8–10.

Russia has begun mass production of the Volna Kupol Garant electronic warfare (EW) system, designed to disrupt Starlink satellite communications.
Russian enterprises are procuring components to produce several hundred more systems, reportedly 300–400 units. Each system is said to cover an area of 15–25 sq. km.
Russia is expected to use these systems to protect key facilities in Ukrainian territories under Russian control from Ukrainian UAVs.

The Armed Forces of Burkina Faso have released footage showing artillery units conducting live-fire exercises using an almost entirely Chinese lineup of fire-support and strike systems.
Equipment seen in the footage:
• Batteries of 122 mm CS/SH1 self-propelled howitzers on Shaanxi 6×6 chassis, with a firing range of 22–27 km;
• 120 mm PLL-05 self-propelled mortars mounted on the Type 92 variant of the WZ551 wheeled chassis, with a firing range of up to 13 km and a digital fire-control system;
• SR-5 (PHL-11) Multiple Rocket Launcher (MRL) on heavy 8×8 chassis, equipped with guided 220 mm rockets with a range of up to 70 km.
In the second part of the video, the Tianlong-30 (Sky Dragon 30) surface-to-air missile (SAM) system was publicly shown for the first time. Its delivery to Burkina Faso had not previously been reported.
The footage shows a launcher and an IBIS-150 three-coordinate radar, capable of detecting targets at ranges of up to 130 km and tracking up to 144 targets. The primary missile is the SD-30, which uses combined guidance and has a reported engagement range of up to 30 km.

The third Dolphin 2-class submarine built for the Israeli Navy, INS Drakon, has departed Kiel for Israel.
The departure ceremony (“Tekes Ha-Shiluach”) was held on August 31 at the Kieler Werft shipyard in Kiel, operated by thyssenkrupp Marine Systems (TKMS).
The INS Drakon has been under construction by TKMS since 2012 and was officially handed over to the Israeli Navy on July 22. It is the largest submarine built in Germany since World War II.
